newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai tops out Futures Building.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai tops out Futures Building.

text.p: The building that will house Shanghai's futures trading has been topped out, the Shanghai Securities News reported on Saturday.

The Shanghai Metals Exchange is investing 800 million yuan in the Shanghai Futures Building in the Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone of the Pudong New Area, which the city wants to turn into its financial centre, it said.
The topping out was completed on Friday on the building, which is 187 metres high, has 37 storeys and a floor area of 71,000 square metres, it said.

Interior work is due to be completed in 1997 and the building will go into operation in 1998, when the Shanghai Metals Exchange will move there, the newspaper said but gave no Shanghai plans to move all its exchanges to Pudong, with the stock market due to go in the middle of 1997.
